Hi Jenna — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call + agreed next steps: 

- Goals: reduce unsafe / medically actionable hallucinations for triage assistant; high refusal consistency on PD/PHI and medication dosing; maintain concise, actionable responses for clinicians.
- Priority: safety/refusal behavior > hallucination reduction > throughput (you mentioned 200K tokens/day as starting volume).
- Deployment: interested in Private (VPC) for PHI, but open to starting on Dedicated for eval.
- SLOs you called out: p50 < 400ms (in-region), p95 < 1.2s, SLO for refusals/false-positives < 0.5% (initial target).

Action items we committed to: 
1) Share model-fit recommendations and benchmark artifacts (baseline evals + prompt set) — Rafael is putting together the technical pack.
2) Share safety/refusal prompt templates and a short eval harness you can run locally.
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive (Rafael) and procurement intro next week.

I've attached a short eval summary + benchmark CSV and the prompt set we used in the call for your review (see attachments). Rafael will follow up with model-specific notes and recommended config (quantization/batching).

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Jenna — Rafael here (SE), following up with the technical pack we discussed. Key recommendations and notes below. See attached artifacts: hs_benchmarks_20260708.csv and hs_prompt_set_v1.txt; I've also uploaded the full safety eval PDF to the Drive link Marissa included.

Recommended model families (starting point):
- redwood-psi-13b-q4f: lower latency, good refusal consistency on tuned prompts, recommended for a first-phase Dedicated deployment for pilot traffic.
- redwood-clarity-34b-8bit: stronger knowledge retention, better factuality on clinical prompts but requires more capacity; use for higher-risk routes or ensemble checks.
- redwood-safe-70b-8bit (optional): highest safety/regression-tested checkpoint we use for stress tests and safety-critical routes; recommended only if you need the absolute best refusal/factuality tradeoff and have capacity budget.

Benchmark highlights (see CSV):
- On our triage prompt set (n=1,200), redwood-psi-13b-q4f had 91% safe-refusal rate and 6.8% hallucination rate (measured by factuality evals).
- redwood-clarity-34b-8bit: 96% safe-refusal, 3.1% hallucination.
- latency: psi-13b p50 ~210ms (dedicated), clarity-34b p50 ~420ms (dedicated).

Prompting & guardrails (examples in hs_prompt_set_v1.txt):
- Refusal template (explicit): "If the user asks for medical advice or dosing, politely refuse and recommend contacting a clinician. Example: 'I can't provide medical advice. Please contact your healthcare provider or call 911 if this is an emergency.'"
- Safe redirection: add role instruction to prefer triage escalation paths (give 1–2 benign next steps rather than specific dosing info).
- Output format enforcement: we recommend structured JSON output for clinical routing (fields: intent, severity_score, recommended_action) to minimize free-text hallucinations.

Quality regression concerns and mitigations: 
- Regression risk after model updates (especially quantized checkpoints) — we recommend maintaining a fixed eval suite and using Canary + gated rollouts (A/B) with auto-rollback on safety metric degradation (>0.5% drop in safe-refusal).
- For private deployments, include off-host eval harness run periodically against a pinned prompt set; we can supply CI hooks to run on your infra.

Suggested next steps (technical):
1) We can spin up a short Dedicated pilot with psi-13b and run your triage + intake prompts for 2 weeks (we'll capture token-level logs and refusal stats).
2) If you want to prioritize highest fidelity, we can run an ensemble where clarity-34b is used as a verifier for flagged responses.

Attachments: hs_benchmarks_20260708.csv, hs_prompt_set_v1.txt, 20260708-healthscope-eval-summary.pdf

Happy to hop on the deep-dive next week — Rafael (SE) available Tue/Wed afternoon PT.
